'''Marc-André "Marco" Zoro Kpolo''' (born 27 December 1983) is an Ivorian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Anyama]], Zoro started his career in Italy, first with [[U.S. Salernitana 1919]], without however making his [[Serie A]] debut. The next season, he played with the [[Campania]] team in the [[Serie B|second division]] and, in January 2003, he joined [[Sicily]]'s [[A.C.R. Messina|F.C. Messina Peloro]], helping them [[2002–03 Serie B|achieve promotion in June]]; the club eventually signed him permanently, on a three-year deal.

Several months prior to the expiration of Zoro's deal with Messina, he and his agent Francis Kacou had been locked in talks for a contract extension.<ref>[http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=30891 Zoro agent set for Messina contract talks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927003049/http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=30891|date=27 September 2007}}</ref> "For Zoro, his contract is coming up to expiration and there are difficulties in getting him to renew", said Messina president Pietro Franza in October 2006.<ref>[http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=15845 Franza unsure over Zoro's Messina deal] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927002851/http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=15845|date=27 September 2007}}</ref> "We will see over the coming days when we meet with his agent if we can find a possible understanding." Four months later, however, Zoro blasted, "I've read that some of the management won't talk to me about a new contract because they want to leave me hanging. I find this an insult to my professionalism. I have always trained hard and never let outside things influence me. I will also leave them hanging and see if the right club comes in for me."<ref>[http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=30158 Zoro furious with Messina contract delays] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070302222807/http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=30158|date=2 March 2007}}</ref><ref>[http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=30702 Zoro: "Don't question my Messina commitment"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071008140623/http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=30702|date=8 October 2007}}</ref> Two days later, he attempted to make amends: "When one of your family is treated poorly, it's normal for that person to be upset. I don't want to air our dirty linen in public. We'll talk about my contract at the end of the season. My priority right now is keeping Messina in Serie A."

On 15 May 2007, Zoro signed a four-year deal with Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica]], arriving [[Free transfer (association football)|for free]]. He would only feature in two [[Primeira Liga]] games throughout the entire [[2007–08 Primeira Liga|campaign]] and eventually was made to train on his own,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/benfica/interior/zoro-o-benfica-e-vieira-trataramme-como-um-cao-1958829.html|title=Zoro: "O Benfica e Vieira trataram-me como um cão!"|trans-title=Zoro: "Benfica and Vieira treated me like a dog!"|publisher=[[Diário de Notícias]]|language=Portuguese|date=22 August 2011|accessdate=29 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202043614/http://www.dn.pt/desporto/benfica/interior/zoro-o-benfica-e-vieira-trataramme-como-um-cao-1958829.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> but scored once in a 2–2 home draw against [[U.D. Leiria]] on 9 March 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.publico.pt/2008/03/09/desporto/noticia/benfica-empata-com-a-uniao-de-leiria-a-dois-golos-1322059|title=Benfica empata com a União de Leiria a dois golos|trans-title=Benfica draw with União de Leiria two goals to two|publisher=[[Público (Portugal)|Público]]|language=Portuguese|date=9 March 2008|accessdate=3 January 2018}}</ref><ref>
[https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01cb-0e6f1fb2041e-548312b3468c-1000--camacho-hands-in-benfica-notice/ Camacho hands in Benfica notice]; UEFA, 9 March 2008</ref> He was transfer-listed in August and, on 10 January 2009, underwent a five-day trial at [[Ewood Park]] with English [[Premier League]] side [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]];<ref>[https://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11676_4776764,00.html Rovers to check on Zoro]; [[Sky Sports]], 10 January 2009</ref><ref>[http://www.slbenfica.pt/Informacao/Futebol/Noticias/noticiasfutebol_furmarczoroemprestimo_090109_43518.asp Zoro no Blackburn Rovers por período experimental (Zoro on trial with Blackburn Rovers)]; S.L. Benfica, 10 January 2009 (in Portuguese)</ref> however, nothing came of it, and he was loaned until the end of [[2008–09 Primeira Liga|the season]] to [[Vitória F.C.]] also in the Portuguese top flight<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dn.pt/desporto/interior/zoro-emprestado-ao-setubal-1127273.html|title=Zoro emprestado ao Setúbal|trans-title=Zoro loaned to Setúbal|publisher=Diário de Notícias|language=Portuguese|date=3 February 2009|accessdate=29 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202043954/http://www.dn.pt/desporto/interior/zoro-emprestado-ao-setubal-1127273.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>– the arrangement was then extended for the entirety of [[2009–10 Primeira Liga|2009–10]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://relvado.aeiou.pt/benfica/benfica-empresta-yebda-freddy-adu-zoro-dabao|title=Benfica empresta Yebda, Freddy Adu, Zoro e Dabao|trans-title=Benfica loan Yebda, Freddy Adu, Zoro and Dabao|publisher=Relvado|first=Susana|last=Valente|language=Portuguese|date=1 September 2009|accessdate=29 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202082011/http://relvado.aeiou.pt/benfica/benfica-empresta-yebda-freddy-adu-zoro-dabao|url-status=dead}}</ref> and he was a regular starter as the ''[[Sado River|Sadinos]]'' again barely avoided relegation.

In late January 2011, Zoro was loaned to [[FC Universitatea Craiova]] of the Romanian [[Liga I]].<ref>[https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/marco-zoro-a-semnat-cu-craiova-226390.html Marco Zoro a semnat cu Craiova (Marco Zoro signed for Craiova)]; [[Gazeta Sporturilor]], 29 January 2011 (in Romanian)</ref> In June, his link with Benfica expired and, on 30 January of the following year he signed a one-and-a-half-year contract with [[Angers SCO]] in the French [[Ligue 2]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/pays-de-la-loire/angers-49000/marc-andre-zoro-sengage-avec-angers-sco-134893|title=Marc-André Zoro s'engage avec Angers Sco|trans-title=Marc-André Zoro joins Angers Sco|publisher=[[Ouest-France]]|language=French|date=30 January 2012|accessdate=29 April 2020}}</ref>

===Racist incidents===
Zoro garnered heavy worldwide interest when, on 27 November 2005, he attempted to stop the Messina–[[Inter Milan]] match by leaving the field with the ball, after being tormented by [[Racism|racist]] taunts from some opposing supporters.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/4476412.stm|title=Zoro suffers more racist abuse|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=27 November 2005|accessdate=10 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/nov/28/europeanfootball.sport|title=Zoro storms off after Inter supporters' racist chanting|work=[[The Guardian]]|first=George|last=Chesterton|date=28 November 2005|accessdate=10 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsId=372816.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120507042611/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsId=372816.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 May 2012|title=Zoro takes a stand on racism|publisher=UEFA|first=Paolo|last=Menicucci|date=28 November 2005|accessdate=10 January 2017}}</ref> He was eventually convinced to keep playing by other players, notably [[Adriano (footballer, born February 1982)|Adriano]] and [[Obafemi Martins]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/2368919/Zoro-fails-to-mask-anger-at-racist-abuse.html|title=Zoro fails to mask anger at racist abuse|publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|first=Richard|last=Bright|date=28 November 2005|accessdate=29 January 2017}}</ref> this then brought strong and unanimous condemnations by the whole football community within Italy, and a five-minute delay for an anti-racism display in all the matches to be played the next week in the country.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.repubblica.it/2005/k/sezioni/sport/calcio/serie_a/razzismo/inritardo/inritardo.html|title=Caso Zoro, il calcio contro il razzismo – Tutte le partite con 5' di ritardo|trans-title=Zoro Affair, football against racism – All matches with five 5-minute delay|publisher=[[La Repubblica]]|language=Italian|date=28 November 2005|accessdate=29 January 2017}}</ref>

The actions of the Inter supporters were also brought to the attention of the European football governing body [[UEFA]], as well as that of the [[European Union]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dw.com/en/european-soccers-racism-problem/a-1798795|title=European soccer's racism problem|publisher=[[Deutsche Welle]]|date=2 December 2005|accessdate=29 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2008/SPORT/football/06/18/racism.europe/index.html?eref=rss_latest|title=Racism still a reality in European football|publisher=[[CNN]]|first=Pedro|last=Pinto|date=20 June 2008|accessdate=29 January 2017}}</ref>

==International career==
Zoro represented the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast national team]] since 2003, and appeared at the [[2006 Africa Cup of Nations]] (where the nation finished second) and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] (no matches played). In the [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations]], he scored his first international goal, in a 3–0 win over [[Mali national football team|Mali]] as the side eventually finished the tournament in fourth position.<ref name=RSSSF>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/ivo-intres0009.html|title=Ivory Coast – Details of International Matches 2000–2009|first=Barrie|last=Courtney|website=[[RSSSF]]|accessdate=8 June 2016}}</ref>

'''Steven Harkness''' (born 27 August 1971) is an English former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] from 1989 to 2002.

Harkness notably played in the [[Premier League]] for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], where he spent a decade before later going on to play in Portugal with [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]. He also played in the [[Football League]] with [[Carlisle United]], [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]], [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] and [[Chester City F.C.|Chester City]].

==Career==

===Carlisle United===
A [[Defender (association football)|defender]] or [[midfielder]], most comfortable at left-back but able to play in a range of positions, he began his career with his hometown club, [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]], signing professional forms on 31 March 1989. After just 13 games for the Cumbrians he impressed sufficiently to be signed by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].

===Liverpool===
He joined under manager [[Kenny Dalglish]] on 17 July [[1989-90 in English football|1989]] for [[Pound sterling|£]]75,000. At this time Liverpool were still the dominant side in England as [[1989 FA Cup Final|holders]] of the [[FA Cup]] and having not finished lower than champions or runners-up in the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] since 1981.

However, Harkness did not walk straight into the first team at [[Anfield]], as [[David Burrows (footballer)|David Burrows]] was the club's first choice left-back. By the time Dalglish resigned on 22 February 1991, Harkness had been at Liverpool for 19 months but had still yet to make his competitive debut. Dalglish was succeeded by [[Graeme Souness]] as Liverpool manager and it was Souness who gave Harkness his Liverpool debut, two years after arriving, in the 1–0 league win over [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] at [[Anfield]] on 27 August 1991 – his 20th birthday. His first goal for the Reds did not come until the 29 April 1995 in the 2–1 league win against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], at [[Carrow Road]]. He was out of the side between December 1994 and mid-April 1995 meaning he missed the victorious [[1995 Football League Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite news
|url=http://www.lfchistory.net/Players/Player/GamesPerSeason/312-36|title=List of appearances in 1994-1995 by Steve Harkness |publisher=lfchistory.net |accessdate=7 February 2017}}</ref>

Harkness suffered a broken leg in Liverpool's 1–0 league defeat at [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]]<ref>{{cite web|author=Articles |url=http://www.lfchistory.net/Articles/Article/802 |title=Harkness is a broken man – LFChistory – Stats galore for Liverpool FC! |publisher=LFChistory |date= |accessdate=6 July 2013}}</ref> on 6 April 1996 and was out of action for nearly a year afterwards. He missed the [[1996 FA Cup Final]], which Liverpool lost 1–0 to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], and also missed the bulk of the [[1996-97 in English football|1996–97 season]], in which Liverpool frequently led the Premier League until being leapfrogged by Manchester United in late January and were ultimately unable to stop their north-west rivals from retaining the league title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liverweb.org.uk/season.asp?season=199596 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071113065544/http://www.liverweb.org.uk/season.asp?season=199596 |archive-date=13 November 2007 |url-status=usurped |title=Liverpool Results 1995–96 |publisher=Liverweb |date= |accessdate=6 July 2013}}</ref>

He made 140 appearances in his six years at the club. He was sent out on loan twice during his Anfield career, firstly to [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]], where he played six times and also [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]], where he, again, played six times. He remained at Anfield until [[1998-99 in English football|1999]] but was one of the first victims of the [[Gérard Houllier]] revolution.

His period at Liverpool was marred by him becoming the first player to be reported to the FA for racist abuse. [[Stan Collymore]] alleged that during a 1998 match for [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] against Liverpool, Harkness subjected him to a 10-minute barrage of insults pertaining to his mixed-race heritage. Harkness denied the allegations.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-harkness-denies-racist-slur-1148631.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-harkness-denies-racist-slur-1148631.html |archive-date=25 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live | location=London | work=The Independent | first=Paul | last=Walker | title=Football: Harkness denies racist slur | date=6 March 1998}}</ref> Later that year in another match between the two teams, Collymore went in with a two-footed challenge on Harkness's standing leg in the ninth minute of the match, causing him to be substituted with injury.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wilson |first1=Paul |title=Stan's the bad man |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1998/nov/21/newsstory.sport28 |accessdate=4 October 2019 |work=The Guardian |date=21 November 1998}}</ref>

===Benfica and Blackburn Rovers===
Harkness left Anfield to join up with old manager [[Graeme Souness]] at [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] on 9 March 1999 for £750,000. He was one of several British players signed for the [[Lisbon]] club by Souness, and chose to wear only his first name on the back of his shirt there.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rainbow |first1=Jamie |title=When Benfica welcomed a British invasion, but wished it hadn't|url=https://www.worldsoccer.com/blogs/when-benfica-welcomed-a-british-invasion-but-wished-it-hadnt-338040 |accessdate=4 October 2019 |work=World Soccer |date=17 November 2012}}</ref> He only lasted five months in Portugal, however, before [[Brian Kidd]] brought him to recently relegated [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in August 1999. The fee was £400,000 with potential add-ons of £100,000.<ref>{{cite news |title=Blackburn agree Harkness fee |url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/news/6112574.blackburn-agree-harkness-fee/ |accessdate=4 October 2019 |work=Lancashire Telegraph |date=24 August 1999}}</ref>

He made his debut for Rovers on 6 November 1999 in the 2–2 league draw with [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] – the first game after Kidd was sacked and long-serving coach [[Tony Parkes]] put in charge – at [[Ewood Park]]. His former Liverpool and Benfica manager Souness was appointed as Blackburn's manager on 15 March 2000.

===Sheffield Wednesday===
After a disappointing year, which saw Blackburn finish mid-table in the [[Football League First Division|First Division]], he was allowed to join [[Sheffield Wednesday]] for £200,000 after just 21 appearances; just like Blackburn when Harkness had joined them a year earlier, Wednesday had just been relegated from the Premier League. His Owls debut came on 30 September 2000 in the 2–0 league defeat to [[Gillingham F.C.|Gillingham]] at the [[Priestfield Stadium]].

His two years at [[Hillsborough Stadium|Hillsborough]] were plagued by injury, however, and he only managed 32 appearances in that time, and scored once against Birmingham City.<ref>{{cite news 
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/983981.stm
|title=Sheff Wed 1–0 Birmingham
|publisher=BBC 
|date=22 October 2000 |access-date=27 October 2009}}</ref> It was not a successful time for the Owls, who narrowly avoided relegation to Division Two in both of his seasons there and would go down the following year. Wednesday terminated his contract in May 2002.<ref>{{cite news |title=One in, one out at Owls |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/s/sheff_wed/2014472.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=29 May 2002 |access-date=24 March 2015 }}</ref>

===Chester City===
Harkness moved to [[Chester City F.C.|Chester City]] on a free transfer on 11 July 2002, playing under former teammate [[Mark Wright (footballer born 1963)|Mark Wright]]. On 1 November that year, aged 31, having played just 10 times due to ankle injury, he ended his contract with the [[Conference Premier]] club by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite news |title=Harkness leaves Chester |url=https://www.cheshire-live.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/harkness-leaves-chester-5309879 |accessdate=4 October 2019 |work=Chester Chronicle |date=1 November 2002}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In September 2019, Harkness admitted at Liverpool Magistrates' Court to driving while disqualified and uninsured. He was sentenced to a three-year driving ban, a nine-week jail term suspended for two years, and 100 hours of community service.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ex-Liverpool FC's Steve Harkness banned from driving |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-49734058 |accessdate=4 October 2019 |publisher=BBC News |date=17 September 2019}}</ref>

'''Nicolás Ignacio Castillo Mora''' (born 14 February 1993) is a Chilean former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]].

==Club career==
===Universidad Católica===
Castillo was born and raised in [[Renca]], suburb of the capital [[Santiago de Chile|Santiago]].<ref name=support>{{Cite news|title=De la galeria a la cancha Nicolás Castillo el delantero de la UC que juega "como hincha"|url=http://www.emol.com/noticias/deportes/2012/06/22/547072/de-la-galeria-a-la-cancha-nicolas-castillo-el-delantero-de-la-uc-que-juega-como-hincha.html|work=Emol|date=23 June 2012|access-date=10 January 2013|first=Felipe|last=Lagos Barahona}}</ref> During his childhood, he was part of [[Club Deportivo Universidad Católica|Universidad Católica]]'s [[supporter groups]]<ref name=support/> and later joined the club's youth ranks when he was 12.<ref name=support/><ref>{{Cite news|title=Nace el Ibra Chileno|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/3522/talentos-de-importaci%C3%B3n/2011/02/01/2332568/talentos-de-importaci%C3%B3n-nicol%C3%A1s-castillo-nace-el-ibra|website=Goal.com|date=1 February 2011|access-date=13 January 2013 }}</ref>

In 2010, Castillo made a goalscorer debut against [[San Pedro de Atacama]] football team for a [[2010 Copa Chile Bicentenario|cup game]], sealing a 10–0 thrash of Católica after scoring the tenth and last goal of it.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nicolás Castillo, el mejor de los mejores|url=http://www.cruzados.cl/futbol/?p=articulo&id=1445|publisher=Cruzados.cl|access-date=9 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140416183249/http://www.cruzados.cl/futbol/?p=articulo&id=1445|archive-date=16 April 2014}}</ref>

In 2011, Castillo debuted professionally in a league match against [[Cobreloa]], coming on as an 84th-minute substitute during a 2–0 win.<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/04/10/chile/primera-division/cd-universidad-catolica/club-de-desportes-cobreloa/1074699/ Universidad Católica vs. Cobreloa 2–0]</ref> On 2 March 2012, he scored his first competitive goal in a 2–0 win over [[Rangers de Talca|Rangers]], again for a league match.<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2012/03/03/chile/primera-division/cd-universidad-catolica/club-social-de-desportes-rangers/1245415/ Universidad Católica vs. Rangers 2–0]</ref>

As a result of his performance in the [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup]], Castillo was linked with [[Premier League]] side [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], where his compatriot [[Ángelo Henríquez]] was playing at the time. Despite the rumours surrounding his move, the transfer never materialised.<ref>{{cite news|title=Transfer news: No Man Utd bids yet for Chile U20 striker Nicolas Castillo|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11065/8826174/transfer-news-no-man-utd-bids-yet-for-chile-u20-striker-nicolas-castillo|publisher=Sky Sports|date=16 July 2013|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref>

===Club Brugge===
In January 2014, Universidad Católica reached an agreement to sell Castillo to [[Belgian Pro League]] side [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]].<ref name="Chilean Zlatan Ibrahimović">{{cite news|title=Cruzados heeft principe-akkoord met Club Brugge over "Chileense Ibrahimovic"|url=http://www.nieuwsblad.be/SportWereld/cnt/DMF20140125_032|publisher=Nieuwsblad|date=25 January 2014|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref> The move became official as Castillo signed for a fee of €3 million on a deal until 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Club Brugge betaalt drie miljoen euro voor Castillo|url=http://www.nieuwsblad.be/SportWereld/cnt/DMF20140127_058|publisher=Nieuwsblad|date=27 January 2014|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref> He scored in his debut for Club Brugge in a 3–1 win over [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]] on 9 February 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=krcgenk 1–3 club brugge kv|url=http://www.nieuwsblad.be/sportwereld/tag/voetbal/jupiler-pro-league-nationaal-2013-2014/krcgenk-club-brugge-kv|publisher=Nieuwsblad|date=9 February 2014|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref> He struggled to score again but did so during the play-offs in the last game of the season against [[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]], with Brugge winning 2–0.<ref>{{cite news|title=Club sluit seizoen af met 2-0 zege tegen Zulte Waregem|url=http://clubbrugge.be/nl/nieuws/18184/matchverslag-club-zulte-waregem|publisher=Official Website of Club Brugge|date=18 May 2014|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref>

On 9 November 2014, Castillo netted a hat-trick in Brugge's 5–0 home win over [[KVC Westerlo|Westerlo]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Sterk Club Brugge legt ook Westerlo over de knie|trans-title=Strong Club Brugge puts Westerlo on its knees|url=http://sporza.be/cm/sporza/matchcenter/mc_voetbal/jupilerleague_1415/JPL_speeldag_15/1.2138800|access-date=23 May 2015|work=Sporza|date=9 November 2014|language=nl|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150419174329/http://sporza.be/cm/sporza/matchcenter/mc_voetbal/jupilerleague_1415/JPL_speeldag_15/1.2138800|archive-date=19 April 2015}}</ref> On 28 January 2015, he was loaned to [[1. FSV Mainz 05]] until the end of the season, with an option to buy.<ref>{{cite news|title=Castillo joins on loan from Brugge|url=http://www.mainz05.de/mainz05/en/aktuell/news/news-detail/article/castillo-kommt-vom-fc-bruegge.html|access-date=23 May 2015|publisher=1. FSV Mainz 05|date=28 January 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150523131836/http://www.mainz05.de/mainz05/en/aktuell/news/news-detail/article/castillo-kommt-vom-fc-bruegge.html|archive-date=23 May 2015}}</ref> On 7 April, having only made one substitute appearance for the [[Bundesliga]] club, he was ruled out for the remainder of the season with damage to his right knee ligaments.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nicolás Castillo se pierde el resto de la temporada en el Mainz|trans-title=Nicolás Castillo to miss rest of season for Mainz|url=http://www.latercera.com/noticia/deportes/2015/04/656-624420-9-nicolas-castillo-se-pierde-el-resto-de-la-temporada-en-el-mainz.shtml|access-date=23 May 2015|publisher=[[La Tercera]]|date=7 April 2015|language=es}}</ref>

Later, on 28 August 2015, Castillo joined Italian side [[Frosinone Calcio|Frosinone]] on loan from Club Brugge until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://football-italia.net/71756/brugges-castillo-frosinone| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150830003903/http://www.football-italia.net/71756/brugges-castillo-frosinone| archive-date = 2015-08-30| title = Brugge's Castillo for Frosinone {{!}} Football Italia}}</ref>

===Pumas===
In 2017, Castillo joined Mexican club [[Club Universidad Nacional|Pumas UNAM]], where he played for a year.

===Benfica===
On 4 June 2018, he was sold to Portuguese side [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], signing a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|last=Rebelo|first=Marco|date=4 June 2018|title=Welcome, Castillo!|url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/en-us/agora/noticias/2017_2018/06/04/futebol-nicolas-castillo-assina-contrato-com-benfica|website=S.L. Benfica|access-date=4 June 2018}}</ref>

===América===
On 1 February 2019, Castillo returned to Mexico, joining [[Club América]] on a €7 million transfer fee, potentially rising to €9 million.<ref>{{cite news|date=31 January 2019|title=Liga MX's Club America signs Chilean striker Nicolas Castillo|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/america/story/3764296/liga-mxs-club-america-signs-chilean-striker-nicolas-castillo|work=ESPN|access-date=2 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=1 February 2019|title=Club América dá as boas-vindas a Castillo|trans-title=Club América welcomes Castillo|url=https://www.abola.pt/Clubes/Noticias/Ver/771427/40|language=pt|work=A Bola|access-date=1 February 2019}}</ref> Nine days later, he made his league debut as a second-half substitute in América's 3–0 loss to [[Club León|León]] at the [[Estadio Azteca]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nicolás Castillo debuta con el América |trans-title=Nicolás Castillo debuts with América |url=https://www.milenio.com/futbol/club-america/nicolas-castillo-debuta-con-el-america |language=es |website=La Afición |date=10 February 2019 |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref>

===Juventude===
On 26 August 2021, Castillo joined Brazilian side [[Esporte Clube Juventude|Juventude]] on loan from América until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nicolás Castillo, nuevo jugador del Juventude de Brasil|url=https://www.record.com.mx/futbol-liga-mx-america/america-nicolas-castillo-nuevo-jugador-del-juventude-de-brasil |language=es |website=Record |date=26 August 2021 |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref>

===Santiago City===
After leaving Universidad Católica in 2024, Castillo signed with [[Santiago City FC|Santiago City]] in the [[Segunda División Profesional de Chile|Chilean Segunda La Liga 2D]] in March 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nico Castillo sorprende a todo Chile con su nuevo club: “Me equivoqué mil veces” |url=https://chile.as.com/videos/un-campeon-de-america-sorprende-a-todo-chile-tras-fichar-en-segunda-division-me-equivoque-mil-veces-v/?pbsvideo=top |access-date=28 March 2025 |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=27 March 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

===City Soccer FC===
On 29 October 2025, Castillo signed with City Soccer FC in the [[United Premier Soccer League|UPSL]].<ref>{{cite instagram |user=citysoccerfl |postid=DQZHJQjDOFZ |title=¡Gran noticia para la familia de City Soccer FC! |date=29 October 2025 |access-date=29 October 2025 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Nicolás Castillo sorprende y se va a la cuarta división de Estados Unidos |url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/Deportes/2025/10/28/1181739/nicolas-castillo-city-soccer-fc.html |access-date=29 October 2025 |work=[[El Mercurio|Emol]] |date=28 October 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

==International career==
Castillo was [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup squads#Chile|listed in the 21-man squad]] for the 2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://peru.com/futbol/la-nueve/mundial-sub-20-turquia-2013-chile-presento-lista-convocados-noticia-142854|title=Mundial Sub 20 Turquía 2013: Chile presentó lista de convocados|publisher=La Nueve|date=3 June 2013|access-date=9 September 2014}}</ref> In the tournament, he scored four goals, including an opener against [[Egypt national under-20 football team|Egypt]], and was the top-scorer for Chile.<ref>{{cite news|title=Egypt lose to Chile in opening Under-20 group match|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23023336|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 June 2013|access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref>

Castillo made his debut for the [[Chile national football team|Chile senior team]] on 23 March 2013 in a 1–0 [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)]] away loss to [[Peru national football team|Peru]], coming on as a 70th-minute substitute for [[Jean Beausejour]].<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/03/23/south-america/wc-qualifying-south-america/peru/chile/1172931/ Peru vs. Chile 1–0]</ref>

In 2016, Castillo was nominated for the [[2016 Copa América]] squad and was part of the Chilean victory in the tournament. He was subbed in the 104th minute of [[Copa América Centenario Final|the final]] against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], which Chile won 4–2 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]], where he converted the 2nd spot kick.

==Post-retirement==
===Football 7===
Once Castillo retired from [[Association football|professional football]] in February 2026,<ref>{{cite news |title=Ni en Chile ni en el extranjero: El drástico final de carrera para Nicolás Castillo tras meses de silencio |url=https://www.alairelibre.cl/futbol/nicolas-castillo-retiro-futbol-profesional-universidad-catolica/ |access-date=2 April 2026 |work=AlAireLibre.cl |publisher=[[Radio Cooperativa]] |date=16 February 2026 |language=es}}</ref> he joined the City Soccer FC [[Seven-a-side football|football 7]] team<ref>{{cite web |title=City Soccer FC |url=https://tst7v7.com/soccer-teams/city-soccer-fc/ |website=TST: The Soccer Tournament |access-date=2 April 2026}}</ref> with views to the 2026 TST Tournament.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Martínez |first1=Nelson |title="Está confirmado para jugar": Nicolás Castillo vuelve a las canchas buscando una millonada |url=https://redgol.cl/internacional/esta-confirmado-para-jugar-nicolas-castillo-vuelve-a-las-canchas-con-una-millonada-en-el-horizonte |access-date=2 April 2026 |work=RedGol |date=2 April 2026 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=City Soccer FC - TST: The Soccer Tournament |url=https://tst7v7.com/soccer-teams/city-soccer-fc/ |website=TST: The Soccer Tournament |access-date=17 September 2026}}</ref>

===Golf===

'''Bruno Cortês Barbosa''' (born 11 March 1987), known as '''Bruno Cortez''', is a Brazilian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]].

Cortez changed his surname spelling from Cortês to Cortez, without circumflex diacritic and with a final ''z'' ending after being asked to do so by the [[Nova Iguaçu Futebol Clube|Nova Iguaçu]] club president.<ref name="With three weeks of São Paulo, Cortês asked to turn 'Cortez'">{{cite web| url=http://sportv.globo.com/site/programas/arena-sportv/noticia/2012/01/com-apenas-tres-semanas-de-sao-paulo-bruno-cortes-vira-cortez.html| title = Com apenas três semanas de São Paulo, Bruno Cortês vira Cortez | date =23 January 2012 | accessdate =23 January 2012 | publisher=Globo Esporte|language=Portuguese }}</ref> After leaving his youth club, Cortez decided to keep the spelling as an ''artistic name''.

==Club career==

===Early career===
Born in [[Rio de Janeiro]],<ref name="Guia">{{Cite journal|journal=Especial Placar Guia 2011 Brasileirão|issue=1354-A|title=Bruno Cortês|date=May 2011|page=52}}</ref> he began his career as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] in 2006, as part of {{ill|Centro de Futebol Arturzinho|lt=Arturzinho|pt|Centro de Futebol Arturzinho}}'s squad.<ref name="orm">{{cite web | title =Lateral da Seleção não deu certo no Paysandu. Saiba mais! | archiveurl =https://web.archive.org/web/20120508122315/http://www.orm.com.br/2009/noticias/default.asp?id_modulo=1087&id_noticia=551936 | url =http://www.orm.com.br/2009/noticias/default.asp?id_modulo=1087&id_noticia=551936 | date =7 September 2011 | archivedate =8 May 2012 | accessdate =4 October 2011 | publisher =Portal ORM | language =Portuguese | url-status =dead}}</ref> He was loaned to [[Paysandu Sport Club|Paysandu]] in 2007, when he played a single game, against [[Tuna Luso Brasileira|Tuna Luso]] in the [[Campeonato Paraense]].<ref name="orm" />

Cortez's first professional contract was with Qatari club [[Al-Shahaniya Sports Club|Al-Shahaniya]] in 2007.<ref name="Guia" /> He moved back to his home country to play for [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro state]]-based club [[Clube Atlético Castelo Branco|Castelo Branco]] from 2008 to 2009,.<ref name="castelobranco">{{cite web | title =Cortês: A jornada até a consagração | url=http://www.trivella.com.br/noticia/22| date =15 December 2011 | accessdate =23 December 2011 | author=Natália Cordeiro| publisher=Trivella|language=Portuguese }}</ref> He left the club to defend [[Quissamã Futebol Clube|Quissamã]], also from Rio de Janeiro state, for the 2009 and 2010 seasons.<ref name="Guia" /> He joined [[Nova Iguaçu Futebol Clube|Nova Iguaçu]] in 2011, playing 14 [[Campeonato Carioca]] games for the club during [[2011 Campeonato Carioca|that season]].<ref name="soccerway">{{cite web | title =Bruno Cortês | url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/bruno-cortes-barbosa/172590| accessdate =12 September 2011 | publisher=Soccerway }}</ref> In March of the same year, Nova Iguaçu received a bid from [[Clube do Remo|Remo]] for the defender but rejected the offer.<ref name="orm" />

===Botafogo===
Rio de Janeiro city-based club [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] acquired 50% of his economic rights after the conclusion of the Campeonato Carioca.<ref name="botafogotosãopaulo">{{cite web | title =Botafogo fecha com Andrezinho e vende Cortês para o São Paulo | url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/noticia/2011/12/botafogo-fecha-com-andrezinho-e-vende-cortes-para-o-sao-paulo.html| date =17 December 2011 | accessdate =17 December 2011 | publisher=Globo Epsorte|language=Portuguese }}</ref> He played 28 [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] games for the club during the [[2011 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2011 season]].<ref name="soccerway" /> Cortez played his first game for the club on 22 May 2011, at [[Teixeirão|Estádio Benedito Teixeira]], in [[São José do Rio Preto]], on a 2–0 defeat against [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]].<ref name="soccerwaydebutbotafogo">{{cite web | title =Palmeiras vs. Botafogo - 22 May 2011 | url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/05/22/brazil/serie-a/sociedade-esportiva-palmeiras/botafogo-de-futebol-e-regatas/1094035/| accessdate =10 October 2011 | publisher=Soccerway }}</ref> He played his last match for Botafogo on 4 December 2011, on a 1–1 tie against [[Fluminense Football Club|Fluminense]] at [[Estádio Raulino de Oliveira]], in [[Volta Redonda]], for the last round of the Série A.<ref name="botafogolastgame">{{cite web | title =Fluminense empata com o Botafogo e se livra da pré-Libertadores | url =http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/campeonatos/brasileiro/serie-a/pos-jogo/2011/12/04/fluminense-empata-com-o-botafogo-e-se-livra-da-pre-libertadores.htm | date =4 December 2011 | accessdate =24 December 2011 | publisher =UOL | language =Portuguese | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20120104091748/http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/campeonatos/brasileiro/serie-a/pos-jogo/2011/12/04/fluminense-empata-com-o-botafogo-e-se-livra-da-pre-libertadores.htm | archive-date =4 January 2012 | url-status =dead}}</ref><ref name="botafogofluminensedecember42011">{{Cite web|url=http://www2.cbf.com.br/sumulas/bofl041211s.pdf|title=Súmula e relatório da partida|publisher=[[Brazilian Football Confederation|Confederação Brasileira de Futebol]]|date=4 December 2011|accessdate=24 December 2011|language=Portuguese|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615160919/http://www2.cbf.com.br/sumulas/bofl041211s.pdf|archivedate=15 June 2012}}</ref>

===São Paulo===
Cortez transfer to Série A club [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] was announced on 17 December 2011,<ref name="botafogotosãopaulo" /> with the contract being signed four days later.<ref name="transfertosãopaulodecember212011">{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/sao-paulo/noticia/2011/12/sao-paulo-anuncia-pacotao-de-natal-com-cinco-nomes-cortes-e-destaque.html| title = São Paulo anuncia pacotão de Natal com cinco nomes, Cortês é destaque | date =21 December 2011 | accessdate =24 December 2011 | publisher=Globo Esporte|language=Portuguese }}</ref><ref name="botafogotosãopaulofoxnews">{{cite web | title =Sao Paulo Signs Defender Cortes | url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/sao-paulo-signs-defender-cortes/| date =22 December 2011|access-date =23 December 2011 | publisher=Fox News }}</ref> He played his first game for the ''Tricolor'' on 22 January 2012, in a 4–0 victory against [[Botafogo Futebol Clube (SP)|Botafogo-SP]] at the [[Estádio do Morumbi]], for the [[Campeonato Paulista]] championship.<ref name="sãopaulodebut">{{cite web| title=Cortês aprova estreia: "Time está se encaixando"| author=Kaue Freitas| url=http://saopaulofc.net/noticias/noticias/campeonato-paulista/2012/1/22/cortes-aprova-estreia-time-esta-se-encaixando/| date=22 January 2012| accessdate=23 January 2012| publisher=saopaulofc.net| language=Portuguese| url-status=dead| archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120124113641/http://www.saopaulofc.net/noticias/noticias/campeonato-paulista/2012/1/22/cortes-aprova-estreia-time-esta-se-encaixando/| archivedate=24 January 2012}}</ref> He scored his first goal for São Paulo on 23 May 2012, against [[Esporte Clube Goiás|Goiás]], at the [[Estádio Serra Dourada]], for [[2012 Copa do Brasil|the year]]'s [[Copa do Brasil]].<ref name="Esposa de Cortez chora com primeiro gol do marido pelo São Paulo">{{cite web | title =Esposa de Cortez chora com primeiro gol do marido pelo São Paulo| url=http://www.gazetaesportiva.net/noticia/2012/05/sao-paulo/esposa-de-cortez-chora-com-primeiro-gol-do-marido-pelo-sao-paulo.html| date =24 May 2012 | accessdate =19 July 2012 | publisher=Gazeta Esportiva|language=Portuguese }}</ref>

In May 2013, after São Paulo knock-off from both the [[2013 Campeonato Paulista|State League]] and [[2013 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]], Cortez was removed from the club's roster by president Juvenal Juvêncio and manager [[Ney Franco]] and, alongside four other players, transfer-listed.<ref>{{cite news|title=Juvenal afasta Cortez, Fabrício, Wallyson e Canete e mais 3 do São Paulo|url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/esporte/2013/05/1276452-juvenal-afasta-cortez-fabricio-wallyson-e-canete-e-mais-3-do-sao-paulo.shtml|accessdate=13 July 2013|newspaper=Folha|date=May 2013|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

====Benfica (loan)====
São Paulo loaned Cortez to Portuguese [[Primeira Liga]] side [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] for a year in July 2013.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ferreira|first=Alder|title=Após afastamento no São Paulo, Cortez é apresentado no Benfica|url=http://spfc.terra.com.br/news.asp?nID=102547|accessdate=13 July 2013|newspaper=SPFC.net|date=12 July 2013|language=Portuguese}}</ref> Arriving at the Portuguese side, he stated that playing in Europe was his opportunity to earn a spot back at the [[Brazilian national football team|Brazilian squad]] and end his two-year absence.<ref>{{cite news|title=Na chegada ao Benfica, Cortez traça seu objetivo: quero voltar à Seleção|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/futebol-portugues/noticia/2013/07/na-chegada-ao-benfica-cortez-traca-seu-objetivo-quero-voltar-selecao.html|accessdate=25 August 2013|newspaper=Globo Esporte|date=July 2013|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

Falling out of favour at [[Jorge Jesus]]' squad, Cortez ended his loan spell on 11 January 2014 and returned to São Paulo. Cortez was reported stating "I'll be eternally thankful to the Portuguese club for everything that they did for me and to Jorge Jesus for the opportunity. It didn't work out due to things that happen in football, but I'm positive that I left with an open door."<ref>{{cite news|title=Sem espaço, Cortez entra em acordo e rescinde seu contrato com o Benfica|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/futebol-portugues/noticia/2014/01/sem-espaco-cortez-entra-em-acordo-e-rescinde-seu-contrato-com-o-benfica.html|accessdate=15 March 2014|newspaper=Globo Esporte|date=January 2014|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

====Criciúma (loan)====
São Paulo loaned Cortez again, this time to [[Criciúma Esporte Clube|Criciúma]] in April 2014 for the duration of the [[2014 in Brazilian football|2014 season]].<ref name=Criciúma>{{cite news|title=Criciúma acerta com Cortez, André Lima e deve fechar com mais reforços|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/noticia/2014/04/criciuma-fecha-com-bruno-cortez-andre-lima-zagueiro-e-outro-lateral.html|accessdate=6 April 2014|newspaper=Globo Esporte|date=2 April 2014|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

====Albirex Niigata (loan)====
On 20 January 2015, Cortez signed a two-year loan deal with [[Albirex Niigata]].<ref>{{cite web|script-title=ja:ブラジル・サンパウロＦＣからコルテース選手 移籍加入内定のお知らせ |language=Japanese |url=http://www.albirex.co.jp/news/top_team/43787|accessdate=20 January 2015|newspaper=Albirex Niigata|date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Ex-Botafogo, Bruno Cortês acerta por dois anos com time do futebol japonês |language=Portuguese |trans-title=Ex-Botafogo, Bruno Cortês signs for two years with team of Japanese football |url=http://extra.globo.com/esporte/ex-botafogo-bruno-cortes-acerta-por-dois-anos-com-time-do-futebol-japones-15099742.html|accessdate=20 January 2015|newspaper=Globo Esporte|date=15 January 2015}}</ref>

===Grêmio===
After two years playing in Japan, Cortez came back to Brazil in 2017 and discussed his contractual rescission with [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]]. At this moment, Cortez prioritize to play in his home country.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cortez volta do Japão e espera sair do São Paulo com rescisão amigável|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/sao-paulo/noticia/2017/01/cortez-volta-do-japao-e-espera-sair-do-sao-paulo-com-rescisao-amigavel.html|accessdate=12 January 2017|newspaper=Globo Esporte|date=January 2017|language=Portuguese}}</ref> He joined [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] shortly after cutting ties with São Paulo.

==International career==
Cortez was called up for the [[Brazil national football team]] to compete against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in both [[Superclásico das Américas]] matches, and was capped for the first time in the 2-0 Brazil victory on 14 September 2011 at the [[Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes]] in [[Córdoba, Argentina|Córdoba]].<ref name="fifaargentinaseptember142011">{{cite web | title =Domestic squad named for Argentina matches | url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1505866.html| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119223921/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1505866.html| url-status=dead| archive-date=19 January 2015| accessdate =12 September 2011 | publisher=[[FIFA]]}}</ref> He also appeared in the second leg on 28 September at the [[Estádio Olímpico do Pará|Mangueirão]] in [[Belém]].<ref name="fifaargentinaseptember282011">{{cite web | title =Os convocados para o Superclássico | url =http://www.cbf.com.br/noticias/selecao-brasileira/2011/9/22/convocacao-para-o-superclassico-(1) | date =22 September 2011 | accessdate =22 September 2011 | publisher =[[Brazilian Football Confederation|CBF]] | language =Portuguese | url-status =dead | archiveurl =https://web.archive.org/web/20110924054026/http://www.cbf.com.br/noticias/selecao-brasileira/2011/9/22/convocacao-para-o-superclassico-%281%29 | archivedate =24 September 2011}}</ref>

(on loan from [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]]) | clubnumber = 20 | youthyears1 = 2007–2016 | youthclubs1 = [[FC Les Lilas|Les Lilas]] | youthyears2 = 2016–2018 | youthclubs2 = [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] | years1 = 2017–2018 | clubs1 = [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse B]] | caps1 = 9 | goals1 = 0 | years2 = 2018–2019 | clubs2 = [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] | caps2 = 10 | goals2 = 1 | years3 = 2019–2021 | clubs3 = [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] | caps3 = 4 | goals3 = 0 | years4 = 2020 | clubs4 = → [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] (loan) | caps4 = 8 | goals4 = 0 | years5 = 2020–2021 | clubs5 = → [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] (loan) | caps5 = 0 | goals5 = 0 | years6 = 2021 | clubs6 = → [[OGC Nice|Nice]] (loan) | caps6 = 15 | goals6 = 1 | clubs7 = [[OGC Nice|Nice]] | years7 = 2021–2025 | caps7 = 100 | goals7 = 1 | clubs8 = → [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] (loan) | years8 = 2024–2025 | caps8 = 27 | goals8 = 0 | years9 = 2025– | clubs9 = [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] | caps9 = 23 | goals9 = 0 | years10 = 2026– | clubs10 = → [[RC Lens|Lens]] (loan) | caps10 = 2 | goals10 = 0 | nationalyears1 = 2018–2019 | nationalteam1 = [[France national under-20 football team|France U20]] | nationalcaps1 = 9 | nationalgoals1 = 0 | nationalyears2 = 2023 | nationalteam2 = [[France national football team|France]] | nationalcaps2 = 2 | nationalgoals2 = 0 | club-update = 22:45, 18 September 2026 (UTC) | nationalteam-update = }} '''Jean-Clair Dimitri Roger Todibo''' (born 30 December 1999) is a French professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[Ligue 1]] club [[RC Lens|Lens]], on loan from [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] ==Early life== Todibo was born in [[French Guiana]] and grew up in the northeastern suburbs of Paris. At nine years old, he was struck by a [[motor vehicle]] with doubts he would walk again, let alone play football.{{cite web |last1=Thomas |first1=Roshane |title=Jean-Clair Todibo's 'miracle' comeback: 'He woke from a coma and said: I'll play football again' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5739298/2024/09/12/jean-clair-todibo-west-ham-coma-miracle/ |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=6 October 2024 |date=12 September 2024 |archive-date=23 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923175908/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5739298/2024/09/12/jean-clair-todibo-west-ham-coma-miracle/ |url-status=live }} He eventually made a full recovery and continued playing with [[FC Les Lilas|Les Lilas]], the club which signed him at six years old. ==Club career== ===Toulouse=== Todibo left Les Lilas for [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] in 2016.{{cite web|url=https://www.lesviolets.com/actu/a-la-decouverte-de-jean-clair-todibo,41328.html|title=À la découverte de Jean-Clair Todibo|trans-title=On the discovery of Jean-Clair Todibo|publisher=Les Violets|date=7 July 2017|language=fr|access-date=19 August 2018|archive-date=6 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190506192146/https://www.lesviolets.com/actu/a-la-decouverte-de-jean-clair-todibo,41328.html|url-status=dead}} He made his [[Ligue 1]] debut on 19 August 2018 against [[Derby de la Garonne]] rivals [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], playing 89 minutes in an eventual 2–1 home win. On 1 September, he was sent off in 26 minutes of a 2–1 win at [[EA Guingamp|Guingamp]].{{cite news |title=Le TFC s'impose à Guingamp 2–1, revivez la victoire des Violets ! |trans-title=TFC impose themselves on Guingamp with a 2–1 win, relive the Violets' victory! |url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2018/08/31/2860129-suivez-en-direct-tfc-guingamp-ce-samedi-a-20-heures.html |access-date=19 February 2019 |work=La Depeche |date=1 September 2018 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190619200104/https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2018/08/31/2860129-suivez-en-direct-tfc-guingamp-ce-samedi-a-20-heures.html |archive-date=19 June 2019 |url-status=dead }} He played ten games for the club and scored once, a late equaliser on 30 September in a 1–1 draw at [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].{{cite news |title=À 10 contre 11, le TFC obtient le nul 1–1 à Rennes en toute fin de match |trans-title=With 10 men against 11, TFC obtain a 1–1 draw at Rennes right at the death |url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2018/09/30/2878896-suivez-rennes-tfc-en-direct-a-partir-de-15-heures.html |access-date=19 February 2019 |work=La Depeche |date=30 September 2018 |language=fr |archive-date=20 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220003042/https://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2018/09/30/2878896-suivez-rennes-tfc-en-direct-a-partir-de-15-heures.html |url-status=live }} ===Barcelona=== On 8 January 2019, Todibo reached an agreement with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] which would see him join them on a free transfer in July 2019, when his contract with Toulouse was due to expire.{{cite news |title=Todibo, Barça's new signing for 2019–20 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/969593/ |access-date=19 February 2019 |publisher=FC Barcelona |date=8 January 2019 |archive-date=8 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108201858/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/969593/ |url-status=live }} However, the Spanish side pushed the transfer forward and he joined the club on 31 January 2019. He became the 22nd French player to sign for Barcelona and was handed the number 6 shirt.{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1010921/jean-clair-todibo-transfer-to-fc-barcelona-brought-forward|title=Jean-Clair Todibo transfer to FC Barcelona brought forward|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=31 January 2019|access-date=31 January 2019|archive-date=22 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422221201/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1010921/jean-clair-todibo-transfer-to-fc-barcelona-brought-forward|url-status=live}} He made only four appearances total for Barcelona. ====Loan to Schalke 04==== On 15 January 2020, Todibo was [[Loan (association football)|loaned]] to [[Bundesliga]] club [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] until the end of the season with a buy option for €25 million, plus €5 million in add-ons.{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1572725/agreement-with-schalke-04-for-todibo-on-loan|title=Agreement with Schalke 04 for Todibo on loan|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=15 January 2020|access-date=15 January 2020|archive-date=15 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115211529/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1572725/agreement-with-schalke-04-for-todibo-on-loan|url-status=live}} In March, Todibo was named Schalke's Player of the Month which was voted by the fans.{{cite web|url=https://www.https/|title=Todibo named Player of the Month|publisher=FC Schalke 04|date=22 March 2020|access-date=23 March 2020|archive-date=19 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819141428/http://https/|url-status=dead}} ====Loan to Benfica==== On 5 October 2020, Todibo joined [[Primeira Liga]] club [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] on a one-year loan with an option to purchase for €20 million.{{Cite web|title=Agreement with Benfica for loan of Todibo|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1856813/agreement-with-benfica-for-loan-of-todibo|access-date=2020-10-09|publisher=FC Barcelona|language=en|archive-date=8 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201008221925/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1856813/agreement-with-benfica-for-loan-of-todibo|url-status=live}} ===Nice=== On 1 February 2021, Todibo joined Ligue 1 club [[OGC Nice|Nice]] on loan with an option to buy after his loan contract was mutually terminated by Barcelona and Benfica.{{Cite web|date=1 February 2021|title=Jean-Clair Todibo signs for OGC Nice|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/en/news/41895/jean-clair-todibo-signs-for-ogc-nice|url-status=dead|access-date=27 June 2021|website=OGC Nice|archive-date=6 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210206051932/https://www.ogcnice.com/en/news/41895/jean-clair-todibo-signs-for-ogc-nice}} On 27 June, the move was made permanent by the club as they paid €8.5m (+ €7m in variables) to Barcelona. Barcelona also reserved rights to a percentage of his future sale.{{Cite web|date=27 June 2021|title=Todibo officially completes permanent move!|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/en/news/43045/todibo-officially-completes-permanent-move-|url-status=dead|access-date=27 June 2021|website=OGC Nice|archive-date=3 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703044713/https://www.ogcnice.com/en/news/43045/todibo-officially-completes-permanent-move-}} On 18 September 2022, he was sent off in a match against '''Sidny Lopes Cabral''' ({{IPA|pt|ˈsid.ni ˈlɔ.pɨʃ kɐ.ˈbɾal|lang}}; born 18 September 2002) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[full-back (association football)|full-back]] for [[Süper Lig]] club [[Trabzonspor]]. Born in the Netherlands, he plays for the [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde national team]].

==Early life==
Lopes Cabral was born in 2002 in the [[Netherlands]]. His parents were both from [[Santiago, Cape Verde|Santiago]], Cape Verde.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |date=2 July 2026 |title=Cape Verde's Sidny Lopes Cabral: 'If you're like “oh, it's Messi”, you're gonna lose your mind' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/02/cape-verde-sidny-lopes-cabral-interview-argentina-lionel-messi-world-cup |access-date=4 July 2026 |work=The Guardian |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> As a youth player, Lopes Cabral joined the youth academy of Swedish side [[Helsingborgs IF|Helsingborg]]. He was regarded as a bright prospect whilst playing for the club's youth team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gasetten.se/helsingborgs-if/de-15-storsta-talangerna-i-hif-snart-kommer-flera-starka-argangar/|title=De 15 största talangerna i HIF: Snart kommer flera starka årgångar|publisher=gasetten.se}}</ref>

==Club career==
In 2024, Lopes Cabral signed for German side [[FC Viktoria Köln|Viktoria Köln]]. He was described as a key part of the club's newfound defensive stability.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ksta.de/sport/viktoria-koeln/mit-viererkette-und-sidny-lopes-cabral-die-neue-stabilitaet-des-fc-viktoria-koeln-733814|title=Die neue Stabilität des FC Viktoria Köln|publisher=Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger|date=7 February 2024}}</ref>

In the summer of 2025, Lopes Cabral moved to Portugal, signing a three-year contract through to 2028 with [[Primeira Liga]] club [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]]. He became an offensive weapon for his new club in his debut season, registering five goals and providing two assists in the league, the highlight being a hat-trick scored in a game away at [[Casa Pia A.C.|Casa Pia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 June 2025 |title=Sidny Cabral é reforço do Estrela da Amadora |trans-title=Sidny Cabral is a Estrela da Amadora reinforcement |url=https://estrelamadora.pt/sidny-cabral-e-reforco-do-estrela-da-amadora/ |access-date=8 December 2025 |publisher=C.F. Estrela da Amadora |language=pt}}</ref>

After impressing during the first half of the season with Estrela, on 30 December 2025, Lopes Cabral joined fellow Primeira Liga side [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], signing a contract until June 2030 for a reported fee of €6 million, which could rise to €8.5 million with add-ons.<ref>{{cite news |date=30 December 2025 |title=Lopes Cabral é reforço do Benfica! |trans-title=Lopes Cabral is a Benfica reinforcement! |url=https://www.slbenfica.pt/pt-pt/agora/noticias/2025/12/30/futebol-benfica-lopes-cabral-reforco-contratacao-ate-2030 |access-date=30 December 2025 |publisher=S.L. Benfica |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=30 December 2025 |title=Benfica: o valor da cláusula de rescisão de Sidny Cabral |trans-title=Benfica: Sidny Cabral's release clause value |url=https://www.abola.pt/noticias/benfica-o-valor-da-clausula-de-rescisao-de-sidny-cabral-2025123022064479053 |access-date=30 December 2025 |publisher=A Bola |language=pt}}</ref> He made his debut on 4 January 2026, coming on as a substitute during the second half and assisting [[Vangelis Pavlidis]] for his hat-trick goal in a 3–1 league victory over [[G.D. Estoril Praia|Estoril]] at the [[Estádio da Luz]].<ref>{{cite news |date=3 January 2026 |title=Sidny e a estreia no Benfica: "Nem sei que dizer!" |trans-title=Sidny and the debut for Benfica: «I don't even know what to say!» |url=https://www.abola.pt/noticias/sidny-e-a-estreia-no-benfica-nem-sei-que-dizer-2026010320205274347 |access-date=4 January 2026 |publisher=A Bola |language=pt}}</ref> On 25 January, Lopes Cabral scored his first goal for Benfica, the third in a 4–0 league victory over his former club Estrela da Amadora.<ref>{{cite news |date=25 January 2026 |title=Lopes Cabral fez primeiro golo pelo Benfica contra... o Estrela: "Foi um bocadinho estranho" |trans-title=Lopes Cabral scored first goal for Benfica against... Estrela: «It was a little bit weird» |url=https://sapo.pt/artigo/lopes-cabral-fez-primeiro-golo-pelo-benfica-contra-o-estrela-foi-um-bocadinho-estranho-69767f4b1b2f4b1aa6cdbbed |access-date=25 January 2026 |website=SAPO |language=pt}}</ref>

In June 2026, Benfica agreed to transfer Lopes Cabral to Turkish club [[Trabzonspor]] for a reported fee of €10 million, with the player arriving in Turkey to complete the move.<ref>{{cite news |date=3 June 2026 |title=Já está na Turquia a primeira venda do Benfica |url=https://www.abola.pt/noticias/ja-esta-na-turquia-a-primeira-venda-do-benfica-video-2026060310340023018 |access-date=4 June 2026 |publisher=A Bola |language=pt}}</ref>

==International career==
Lopes Cabral was first called up to the [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde national team]] for a [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] against [[Comoros national football team|Comoros]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thueringer-allgemeine.de/sport/fussball/regionalliga/article239736589/Sidny-Cabral-vom-FC-Rot-Weiss-Erfurt-vor-Debuet-im-Nationaltrikot.html|title=Sidny Cabral vom FC Rot-Weiß Erfurt vor Debüt im Nationaltrikot|publisher=thueringer-allgemeine.de}}</ref> He scored his first international goal on 29 May 2025, in a friendly against [[Malaysia national football team|Malaysia]] at the [[Kuala Lumpur Stadium]].<ref name="NFT"/>

On 18 May 2026, Lopes Cabral was selected by Cape Verde head coach [[Bubista]] for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], the nation's first ever appearance at the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/cabo-verde-squad-announcement-world-cup-bubista |title=Cabo Verde announce squad for historic maiden World Cup |publisher=FIFA |date=18 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/fifa-world-cup-2026/articles/bubista-s-official-cabo-verde-squad-for-the-2026-fifa-world-cup-2026-05-19|title=Bubista’s Official Cabo Verde Squad For The 2026 FIFA World Cup|website=beIN SPORTS|date=19 May 2026}}</ref> In Cape Verde's [[2026 FIFA World Cup round of 32|round of 32]] match against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] on 3 July, Lopes Cabral scored a second equalizing goal for his side with a curling shot in the first half of [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elcomercio.pe/deporte-total/futbol-mundial/gol-de-lopes-cabral-hoy-con-cabo-verde-vs-argentina-por-dieciseisavos-del-mundial-2026-gol-de-cabo-verde-ultimas-noticia/|title=Gol de Lopes Cabral hoy con Cabo Verde vs. Argentina por dieciseisavos del Mundial 2026|access-date=4 July 2026|date=3 July 2026|publisher=El Comercio|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Walker-Roberts |first=James |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/football/world-cup/2026/sidny-cabral-goal-cabo-verde-argentina-best_sto23316037/story.shtml |title=An all-time great World Cup goal - Watch Sidny Cabral's 'unbelievable' strike against Argentina in thrilling last-32 game |publisher=TNT Sports |date=4 July 2026 }}</ref> Although Cape Verde went on to lose the match 3–2, Lopes Cabral's strike would be voted the [[FIFA World Cup awards#Goal of the Tournament|best goal of the tournament]].<ref name="GOTT">{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/sidny-lopes-cabral-cabo-verde-goal-tournament|title=Lopes Cabral gem wins Goal of the Tournament|access-date=27 July 2026|date=27 July 2026|publisher=FIFA}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Lopes Cabral mainly plays as a defender, and can operate as a left-back or right-back.

==Personal life==
Lopes Cabral's older brother [[Rodny Lopes Cabral|Rodny]] also played for the Cape Verde national team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.voetbalzone.nl/nieuws/afvaller-van-fc-twente-duikt-op-bij-zesvoudig-kampioen-kippenvel/386776|title=Afvaller van FC Twente duikt op bij zesvoudig kampioen: 'Kippenvel'|publisher=Voetbalzone}}</ref>
